title: Smooth connected cocharacter limit groups and their Lie weights
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $F$, and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga] for commutative $F$-algebras $A$. Lie algebras are tangent spaces at the identity, with the adjoint action obtained by differentiating conjugation. Let $G$ be smooth and connected and $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to G$ a group homomorphism. Define $P_\lambda(A)$ to consist of $g\in G(A)$ for which $t\mapsto\lambda(t)g\lambda(t)^{-1}$ extends to a morphism $\mathbf A^1_A\to G_A$. Define $U_\lambda(A)$ by requiring in addition that this extension has value $1$ at $0$. Define $Z_\lambda(A)$ to consist of $g\in G(A)$ such that $g_{A'}$ commutes with $\lambda(s)$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $A'$ and every $s\in(A')^\times$. Then $P_\lambda,U_\lambda,Z_\lambda$ are represented by smooth connected closed subgroups of $G$, $U_\lambda$ is normal in $P_\lambda$, and multiplication induces an isomorphism of group schemes $U_\lambda\rtimes Z_\lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}P_\lambda$. Here the semidirect product has underlying scheme $U_\lambda\times_F Z_\lambda$ and multiplication $(u,z)(u',z')=(u z u' z^{-1},zz')$. The group $U_\lambda$ is unipotent, meaning that in a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation all its geometric points $u$ satisfy $(u-I)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. If $\mathfrak g_n=\{v\in\operatorname{Lie}(G):\operatorname{Ad}(\lambda(t))v=t^n v\}$ denotes the integer-character weight space, the weight decomposition and tangent subspaces are
$$\operatorname{Lie}(G)=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\mathfrak g_n,\qquad\operatorname{Lie}(Z_\lambda)=\mathfrak g_0,\qquad\operatorname{Lie}(U_\lambda)=\bigoplus_{n>0}\mathfrak g_n,\qquad\operatorname{Lie}(P_\lambda)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathfrak g_n.$$
These are equalities of subgroup functors on all commutative test algebras and of their tangent subspaces, not just assertions on geometric points.

source.place: Definition 13.21 and Propositions 13.23--13.24, printed pp.261--262; Proposition 13.29 and the definitions of P, U and Z, printed pp.263--264; Theorem 13.33(a)--(c),(e), printed pp.265--266; Example 14.13, printed p.283.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-central-torus-faithful-weight-blocks] with $H=G$ and the trivial central torus $T=1=\mathbf G_m^0$ to choose a closed immersion $G\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(V)$ with $\dim V=N>0$. Apply [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] to the representation obtained by composing $\lambda$ with this immersion. Choose its weight basis, ordered so $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_N$. In these coordinates conjugation sends a matrix entry $g_{ij}$ to $t^{m_i-m_j}g_{ij}$. For every $F$-algebra $A$, this Laurent polynomial is polynomial precisely when $g_{ij}=0$ for $m_i<m_j$. The limit is block diagonal, with blocks indexed by equal $m_i$. Since the matrix is block upper triangular and invertible, these diagonal blocks are invertible over $A$. Thus the extended matrix lies in $\operatorname{GL}_N(A[t])$. Its value at zero is $I$ precisely when every diagonal block is $I$. Commutation with the universal unit $t\in A[t,t^{-1}]^\times$ says precisely that entries with $m_i\ne m_j$ vanish. These tests work over arbitrary $A$, by coefficient comparison in Laurent polynomials.

source.place: Theorem 13.33 proof, p.266, faithful embedding and diagonal coordinates; Theorem 12.12, pp.234--235.

proof.text: The equations from step 1 give closed subschemes of $G$ representing $P_\lambda,U_\lambda,Z_\lambda$: they are the intersections with the respective block upper triangular, identity-block upper triangular, and block diagonal matrix subschemes. Indeed an extension in the ambient general linear group factors through $G$: every equation of the closed immersion vanishes after inverting $t$, hence already in $A[t]$, since $A[t]\hookrightarrow A[t,t^{-1}]$ is injective. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-concentrator] to the conjugation action on $X=G$, first with $Z=G$, then with $Z=\{e\}\simeq\operatorname{Spec}F$. Both invariant subschemes are smooth, so $P_\lambda$ and $U_\lambda$ are smooth. The block diagonal intersection represents the fixed subfunctor for conjugation by $\mathbf G_m$, including the universal base-extension test. Therefore [lem-sfb-torus-fixed-scheme-smooth] with $T=\mathbf G_m$ makes $Z_\lambda$ smooth. The same arguments apply to $-\lambda$.

Uniqueness of polynomial extension shows that products and inverses of orbit extensions are the extensions for products and inverses. Hence $P_\lambda$ is a subgroup and evaluation $q:P_\lambda\to G$ at zero is a group homomorphism. In the coordinates of step 1 its image is block diagonal, so factors through $Z_\lambda$, and it is the identity on $Z_\lambda$. Its kernel on every test algebra is $U_\lambda$, proving normality. The maps $(u,z)\mapsto uz$ and $g\mapsto(gq(g)^{-1},q(g))$ are inverse scheme morphisms between $U_\lambda\times Z_\lambda$ and $P_\lambda$. Multiplying $uz$ and $u'z'$ gives $(u(zu'z^{-1}))(zz')$, which is exactly the stated semidirect-product law.

Apply [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] to the differentiated conjugation action on $\mathfrak g=T_eG$, obtaining the finite direct sum of its integer-character spaces. A tangent vector is a point over $D=F[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ reducing to $e$; in the embedding it is $I+\epsilon v$. Conjugation has tangent part $\sum_n\epsilon t^n v_n$. Its orbit extends over $\mathbf A^1_D$ exactly when $v_n=0$ for $n<0$, and the limit is $e$ exactly when also $v_0=0$. Its orbit is constant exactly when $v_n=0$ for every $n\ne0$. The closed-immersion factorization argument of step 2 applies over $D$ too. Thus these three conditions compute respectively $T_eP_\lambda,T_eU_\lambda,T_eZ_\lambda$ as the stated subspaces of $T_eG$. For $-\lambda$ the weights reverse, so $T_eU_{-\lambda}=\bigoplus_{n<0}\mathfrak g_n$.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(c), dual-number calculation and equations (87)--(89), pp.265--266.

proof.text: The equations of step 1 embed $U_\lambda$ into the upper unitriangular matrices: equal-weight blocks are identities and only strictly weight-decreasing off-diagonal blocks can be nonzero. Thus $u-I$ is strictly upper triangular and $(u-I)^N=0$ for every geometric point. Restriction of the chosen closed immersion to $U_\lambda$ is faithful. This proves unipotence with precisely the meaning required in the statement, without a change of representation or a restriction on the characteristic.

source.place: Example 14.13, printed p.283, and the block calculation in Theorem 13.33, p.266.

proof.text: Let $H=U_{-\lambda}$ and $K=P_\lambda$. In step 1's ordered basis, $H$ has identity diagonal blocks and strictly lower off-diagonal blocks, whereas $K$ is block upper triangular. Consequently $H\cap K=1$ on every commutative test algebra. Step 4 gives $\operatorname{Lie}(H)\oplus\operatorname{Lie}(K)=\mathfrak g$. Both groups are smooth by step 2, so [lem-sfb-transverse-subgroup-product-open] gives an open immersion $U_{-\lambda}\times P_\lambda\hookrightarrow G$.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(d), printed p.266, used as in the source to prove (e).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], $G$ is regular. It is connected by hypothesis and nonempty because of its identity, so [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] makes $G$ integral, in particular irreducible. The nonempty open subscheme of step 6 is therefore irreducible and connected. Projection $U_{-\lambda}\times P_\lambda\to P_\lambda$ has the section $p\mapsto(e,p)$, hence is surjective on topological spaces. Its continuous image proves $P_\lambda$ connected. Evaluation $q:P_\lambda\to Z_\lambda$ also has a section, so proves $Z_\lambda$ connected. Finally the morphism $P_\lambda\to U_\lambda$, $g\mapsto gq(g)^{-1}$, has section the inclusion $U_\lambda\hookrightarrow P_\lambda$ and proves $U_\lambda$ connected. All three are already smooth closed subgroups, and all constructions and tangent calculations were performed on arbitrary algebras.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(e), printed p.266; Stacks Tags 056S, 0569 and 033N for regularity and irreducibility.

I read Milne iAG2017 printed pp.261-266 (Def 13.21, Props 13.22-13.30 with Lemmas 13.25-13.27, Examples 13.31-13.32, Thm 13.33 and its proof). I also read every cited statement and the only citer, lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description step 1. The item statement matches Thm 13.33(a)-(c),(e) and Prop 13.29 and is unchanged. Step 1: the central-torus node with T=1 gives a faithful closed immersion and the weight-basis node gives ordered weights m_i; I checked the t^{m_i-m_j} entry criterion, that the diagonal blocks are invertible via det, and the universal-unit test for Z over arbitrary A. Step 2: the extension factors through G by injectivity of A[t] into A[t,t^-1]; the concentrator node with Z=G and Z={e} gives P and U smooth; the torus-fixed node with T=G_m gives Z smooth. Step 3: the evaluation homomorphism q, its kernel U, the inverse maps and the semidirect law all check (Milne's printed domain G corrected to P). Step 4: the dual-number computation gives T_eP, T_eU, T_eZ and the reversal for -lambda. Step 5: U is unitriangular in the faithful embedding. Step 6: U_{-lambda} and P_lambda meet trivially on every A and their Lie algebras are complementary, so the transverse node applies. Step 7: regular plus connected gives integral, the big cell is irreducible, and the sections of the projections carry connectedness to P, Z and U. New node lem-sfb-smooth-affine-concentrator is Milne 13.21-13.24; I tested it on the trivial action, Z empty, and A^1 with weights +1 and -1. New node lem-sfb-transverse-subgroup-product-open is true: the map is a monomorphism, the tangent isomorphism translates to every point, so it is etale, and an etale monomorphism is an open immersion. Neither new node duplicates projective-attracting-cells, torus-fixed-scheme-smooth, smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation or the orbit-geometry nodes (those need a connected acting group and give no open immersion). Both are strictly smaller than the item and are statement-only with four search kinds recorded. No SGA is cited. Accepted tool_uses: lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular and lem-sc-regular-connected-integral, both generic scheme facts used in step 7. The two Milne p.266 slips noted in the report are real (T_ii=0 should be 1; domain G should be P). No fixes.
